activities.title: Mirror face time
activities.whyItWorks: High-contrast face image at optimal focal distance activates developing face-detection circuits without requiring fine visual acuity.

activities.title: Black-and-white card gallery
activities.whyItWorks: High-contrast patterns are the most robustly processed visual stimuli in the 0–2 month window, directly matching the infant visual system's sensitivity profile.

activities.title: Slow object tracking
activities.whyItWorks: Repeated tracking practice strengthens the cortical smooth-pursuit pathways being laid down in real time.

activities.title: Light and shadow play
activities.whyItWorks: Luminance contrast and moving edges are the two most salient visual stimuli for the neonatal visual system — this directly targets the circuits that are active earliest.

activities.title: Tummy time on your chest
activities.whyItWorks: Prone positioning requires active neck extension — even attempts count — and the familiar sound of your heartbeat and voice provides a calming context.

activities.title: Slow sway and narrate walk
activities.whyItWorks: Gentle linear and rotational motion activates semicircular canal pathways — the vestibular system develops early and responds well to slow rhythmic input.

activities.title: Palmar grasp practice
activities.whyItWorks: Each reflex activation is a neural circuit firing — repeated activation strengthens the pathways that will eventually become voluntary grasping.

activities.title: Cloth texture exploration
activities.whyItWorks: Different textures activate distinct mechanoreceptor populations, providing varied somatosensory input to a cortex hungry for calibration data.

activities.title: Scent cloth settling
activities.whyItWorks: Newborns navigate their world largely by smell in the first weeks. Familiar olfactory cues activate stress-buffering responses and demonstrate early associative learning.

activities.title: Gentle joint compression
activities.whyItWorks: Joint compression activates deep proprioceptors that give the brain information about body position — the data source for building a body map.

activities.title: Varied carrying positions
activities.whyItWorks: Different orientations activate different semicircular canals and otolith organs, giving the vestibular cortex varied input to calibrate against.

activities.title: Gentle limb movement
activities.whyItWorks: Movement generates proprioceptive signals that train the brain's maps of the body — even passive movement provides the input the motor cortex uses to calibrate.

activities.title: Water sound bath
activities.whyItWorks: Warm water provides simultaneous activation of thermoreceptors, mechanoreceptors, and proprioceptors across the entire body — among the richest multi-modal sensory experiences available at home.

activities.title: Skin-to-skin time
activities.whyItWorks: Skin-to-skin contact simultaneously activates thermoregulatory, tactile, olfactory, and auditory pathways. It is caregiving and neurostimulation at the same time.

activities.title: Face gazing — the slow face
activities.whyItWorks: Contingent responsiveness — your reaction following their cue — is the fundamental unit of social-brain wiring in this period.

activities.title: The conversation turn
activities.whyItWorks: Pausing and waiting teaches the temporal structure of conversation — turn-taking is a learned social-cognitive pattern, and 0–3 months is when its scaffolding begins.

activities.title: Voice mapping
activities.whyItWorks: Auditory localisation requires coordinating binaural timing differences — this simple activity is actively exercising those circuits.

activities.title: Singing the same song
activities.whyItWorks: Repeated exposure to the same prosodic sequence builds auditory memory traces — the first building blocks of pattern recognition and predictive processing.

activities.title: Reading aloud — anything
activities.whyItWorks: Continuous natural speech exposure provides the prosodic data the auditory cortex is actively seeking and storing in this period.

activities.title: Heartbeat sound settling
activities.whyItWorks: Familiar prenatal sounds trigger auditory memory traces and activate calming responses — one of the earliest examples of long-term memory from in-utero experience.

activities.title: Name repetition at close range
activities.whyItWorks: Repeated pairing of name with face, touch, and context begins building the neural representation that will later allow the infant to recognise their own name from across a room.

activities.title: Hum and chest feel
activities.whyItWorks: Sound delivered simultaneously through air (auditory) and bone conduction (vibrotactile) activates two sensory modalities at once, exercising the cross-modal integration circuits that are building throughout this period.

activities.title: Outdoor ambient listening
activities.whyItWorks: Real-world acoustic environments contain complex, layered sounds the brain must learn to parse — exposure to this richness supports the auditory cortex's statistical learning work.

activities.title: The narrated day
activities.whyItWorks: Continuous natural speech exposure provides the prosodic data the auditory cortex is actively seeking and storing — and every response you give to baby's cues teaches them that their actions matter.

activities.title: Facial expression copying
activities.whyItWorks: Whether or not early imitation is true mimicry, face-to-face contingent interaction at close range activates social and visual processing circuits simultaneously.

activities.title: Contingency mobile (DIY)
activities.whyItWorks: When baby discovers their movement causes the mobile to move, they are learning contingency — that their actions have effects — which is the root of intentional behaviour and early problem-solving.

activities.title: Attention recovery wait
activities.whyItWorks: Gaze aversion is the infant's primary self-regulatory tool. When caregivers wait and return, they teach the brain that the world is safe to re-engage with — foundational for attention and stress regulation.

activities.title: Quiet alert window observation
activities.whyItWorks: Environmental scanning during quiet alert state is active cognitive work — the infant's attention system is calibrating visual salience, contrast, and novelty without any additional input required.

activities.title: Novel object pause
activities.whyItWorks: Renewed attention to novelty is the brain signalling 'this is new' — evidence the memory trace for the first object was encoded. You are watching memory and recognition in real time.
